label: household economics profile
fullDescription: Studies household behaviour and applied econometrics, including household consumption, saving and labour supply, life-cycle models and risk sharing (formal and informal). Research covers evaluation and design of policies in developing countries—education financing, conditional cash transfers, scholarships, micro-credit—and human capital accumulation and early-childhood development, plus measurement issues and survey tools.

snippets.text: Research interests include household consumption, saving and labour supply behavior, risk sharing, evaluation and design of policies in developing countries, human capital accumulation in developing countries, early years interventions, micro-credit, and measurement tools in surveys.

He has carried out evaluations of education financing and access programmes, including large conditional cash transfer programs, the impact of scholarships on school enrolment, and the effect of subjective expectations on the returns to education.

Much of my research has looked at life-cycle models of individual behaviour and their implications for aggregate fluctuations, I have also worked on models of individual interactions, in particular, on formal and informal insurance by households, in developed and developing countries.
I am interested in modelling household behaviour in developed and developing countries and, more generally, in Applied Econometrics.
Recently I have been particularly interested in the process of child development and in measurement issues in economics.

label: emotion and stress psychophysiology lab
fullDescription: Studies embodiment: how the mind and body influence each other during emotion and stress. Specific topics include how emotions change across development and aging, how acute and chronic stress shape decisions and cognition, how discrimination and stigmatization affect physical and mental health, and how affect contagion operates in dyads and groups; the lab uses psychophysiology measures (e.g., heart rate, impedance cardiography, blood pressure, skin temperature, pulse transit time, skin conductance, sleep actigraphy) and techniques such as autonomic physiology, neuroendocrinology, and facial EMG.

snippets.text: Some recent research examines the influence of emotion on decision-making, how discrimination and stigmatization affect physical and mental health, how dyads and groups influence each other in a process called affect contagion, and how stress affects physiology and cognition across the life span.
We study embodiment: how the mind influences the body, and how bodily changes influence thoughts, emotions, and intentions.

For example, we study how emotions are experienced differently along the developmental trajectory, how aging influences risk perceptions and risk taking, how decisions are influenced by acute and chronic stress, and how people manage and attempt to control their racial biases - how those regulatory attempts often fail - resulting in revealing greater racial bias.

label: instrument prototyping facility
fullDescription: Provides a fabrication facility and design support for custom instrumentation, including designing instruments and parts for research groups across campus and educating researchers about modern prototyping techniques.

snippets.text: At the Yale Wright Laboratory Advanced Prototyping Center (APC), our mission is to provide a fabrication facility and design support for custom instrumentation.
We have designed instruments and parts for groups across campus.
We also aim to help researchers develop design skills and educate them about modern prototyping techniques.

label: cancer metabolomics lab
fullDescription: Studies sex-specific differences in metabolism that influence colorectal (colon) cancer etiology, progression, and therapeutic response; integrates metabolomics with research on environmental exposures, birth cohorts, early-onset colorectal cancers, and the microbiome to assess biological responses to exposures. Develops and applies high-resolution mass spectrometry–based metabolomics and bioinformatic protocols (including normalization methods for dried blood spots and urine) and uses epidemiologic techniques to adjust for confounding.

snippets.text: In addition, our research integrates metabolomics analysis with studies on environmental exposures, birth cohorts, early-onset cancers, and microbiome, to understand biological responses to exposures in various contexts.
The laboratory aims to develop a deeper understanding of sex-specific differences in metabolism that influence colorectal cancer etiology, progression, and response to therapeutics.
Our lab has developed several analytical and bioinformatic protocols to enable a comprehensive analysis of the metabolome using high resolution mass spectrometry.
Most recently we have optimized protocols for normalization of metabolites in various matrices from clinical samples, including dried blood spots and urine.
We also adjust for confounding using epidemiologic techniques, as shared factors could influence the metabolome and exposure measured.
The role of metabolites in colon cancer
To address this issue and setup a robust experimental protocol for DBS metabolomics, we assessed the performance of various normalization methods.

label: bioinformatics support program
fullDescription: Provides bioinformatics support and instruction for analysis, functional annotation, and visualization of Next Generation Sequencing and other omics data; performs analyses of bulk and single-cell ChIP-, ATAC-, RNA-seq, and microarray data; conducts enrichment (pathway and network) analysis and visualization of differentially regulated molecules; assists with finding and using public omics datasets, selection of appropriate bioinformatics software/databases, and in‑silico hypothesis development.

snippets.text: The Bioinformatics Support Program provides free access to state-of-the-art commercial bioinformatics software programs and databases for the mining, analysis, functional annotation, and visualization of Next Generation Sequencing data such as Partek Flow, Qlucore Omics Explorer, Ingenuity Pathway Analysis, Ingenuity Variant Analysis, Clarivate Drug Intelligence, Biocyc, and TRANSFAC.
